kana.title: Kana and sound
kana.body: English spelling is not a reliable pronunciation guide. Shi, chi, tsu and fu label kana; the IPA shows the intended sound.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

mora.title: Morae and length
mora.body: Do not replace a long vowel with English word stress. The extra vowel or consonant duration is part of the word.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

loanwords.title: Katakana words
loanwords.body: A loanword may sound different from its English source: コーヒー has two long vowels. English spelling is not an accepted typed answer.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

greetings.title: Greetings and politeness
greetings.body: Japanese greetings depend on context and politeness. Do not assume that one English goodbye maps to every Japanese parting phrase.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

clarification.title: Asking for help
clarification.body: A polite request such as もう一度お願いします does not need an English-style subject or auxiliary.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

copula.title: Topics and polite noun sentences
copula.body: は marks a topic; it is not the verb is. です comes at the end of a polite noun sentence. This is a starting pattern, not a claim that every sentence needs は or a stated subject.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

residence.title: Origin and residence
residence.body: Japanese places the particle after the noun: 東京に, in Tokyo. Do not copy English preposition order.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio

numbers.title: Numbers and age
numbers.body: A bare number is not automatically the form used before a counter. Age one is いっさい, not いちさい. Use Japanese input; English number words and romanisation are not answers.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio
